passage:
At five, Suraj lay flat on the living-room rug ten minutes after putting away his toy cars. "I'm bored. What can I do? Can I use the tablet?" Mummy Sabina handed him a tin of odd spoons, a ball of wool and two chairs. "Make a road." Suraj sighed loudly. Then he wound the wool round the chair legs into a web and drove a spoon down it. Half the morning went by.
At nine, Suraj came in from the garden with a pot he was told to wash. "Ugh! It smells so bad." He held it at arm's length and scrunched his nose. In the evening, Asif Sir showed the class a jar of water with a pinch of salt and a paper clip on the surface. Suraj frowned, then his eyes widened. "Aha! The salt makes the water push up, so the clip floats!" He jumped up. Asif Sir clapped. "That click of understanding is what scientists love. Tell us how you worked it out." Suraj explained it in three sentences and sat down glowing.

qa.q: What did Mummy Sabina give Suraj to make a road?
qa.a: She gave him a tin of odd spoons, a ball of wool and two chairs.

qa.q: How do Suraj's sounds at nine relate to the boredom at five?
qa.a: At five his boredom became a game once he was given time and simple things. At nine, his "Ugh!" showed disgust at the smelly pot, while his "Aha!" marked a sudden click of understanding that Asif Sir celebrated.

qa.q: What was Suraj feeling when he said "Aha!" in Asif Sir's class?
qa.a: He felt excited and proud, because the idea suddenly made sense to him.

qa.q: What could Asif Sir do next to build on Suraj's discovery?
qa.a: He can ask Suraj to test another object in the jar, and invite him to explain his idea to the class.

grounding: A child's boredom that becomes play (4068) and a school-age child's 'ugh' at a chore and 'aha' at a discovery (2370): one boy across years.
